sections.h2: Ways to sell a Princeton house
sections.html:
Princeton owners can put the house on the market with an agent, find a buyer alone, or accept an investor's as-is bid. The open market tends to pay best for a house in good shape. The investor offer wins on speed.

Princeton sits in Collin County and has outgrown nearly every Texas peer. Residents numbered 6,807 in 2010 and 17,027 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate stands at 43,524. Fresh subdivisions mean shoppers can always find a newer house down the road, so your pricing and presentation carry real weight.

  • Open-market listing: the biggest audience, paired with inspection haggling and a lender's schedule.
  • Sale without an agent: the commission stays with you, and so do the contract and every phone call.
  • As-is investor offer: skip the showings and the repair list, then name your own closing day.

About three in four Princeton homes are lived in by their owners; the rest are rentals. Most figures below are 2020-2024 estimates for the city.

Princeton city housing and household figures

Renting costs $2,239 and owning with a loan costs $2,279, nearly the same. A landlord here can fairly ask whether the rental is worth more as income or as cash from a sale.

Owners without a mortgage spend about $566 a month. Carrying a paid-off house is cheap, which gives a debt-free seller room to accept a lower, faster offer.

sections.h2: Using the City of Princeton website
sections.html:
Start at the city's own site when you need to pay a utility bill, report a problem, pay a court fine or read an agenda. It also helps you book the final meter reading and see what the council is debating.

  • Utility payments and account changes, needed to shut off service in your name at sale.
  • Report a Problem, handy for a dead street light by your lot.
  • Agendas, minutes and live meetings, where rezoning and street plans show up.
  • Major Projects, a list of work that may change traffic or the neighbors.

The city also posts public meetings on regional transportation, held with the North Central Texas Council of Governments. A road project near your block deserves a call to city staff before you pick an asking price, because shoppers will find the same plans online.

sections.h2: What does a Princeton owner pay in property tax?
sections.html:
Collin Central Appraisal District sets each home's value. Several local units then apply their own rates, and the district's taxing-entities page shows every unit's exemptions and rates.

  • Value date: January 1, which also starts the year's tax lien.
  • Bills: mailed from about October 1 and due by January 31 for most owners.
  • Delinquency: February 1, with penalty and interest running from that day.
  • School exemption: $140,000 comes off a homestead's school taxable value, plus $60,000 more at age 65 or older or with a disability.

The county's tax office sits at 900 E. Park Blvd, Ste 100, Plano, TX 75074, and answers at 972-881-3014. Request your current balance there before fixing a closing date, because a missed year stays attached to the house. If you never filed for a homestead and the sale closes after January 1, the new owner may still apply for what is left of that year.

Normally the title company delivers the deed to the Collin County clerk. Property Code 12.001(b) lets the clerk accept it only if a notary acknowledged the signature or two witnesses swore to it.

The clerk charges $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every additional page, plus records charges. An inherited house changes the paperwork. Depending on the estate you may record an affidavit of death for a transfer on death deed, an executor's deed after administration, or the will and court order under a muniment of title. The clerk's office can tell you what your case calls for.

sections.h2: Selling when a foreclosure date is close
sections.html:
When a default letter arrives, you have 20 days to pay the overdue amount and halt the process. After that the lender sends a sale notice, and it has to reach you at least 21 days ahead of the first-Tuesday auction.

Ask your lender for a payoff figure and set it against a sale price you could actually get. Selling for enough to cover the loan protects your equity and avoids a deficiency suit, which can follow a foreclosure sale for up to two years.

  • Keep the notice of sale and recent loan statements together.
  • Request a payoff estimate from a title company.
  • Settle what happens with any tenants before closing.

This process runs between you, the lender and the county, so City Hall cannot pause it. Watch for the notice posted at the county clerk.

sections.h2: How an as-is sale unfolds, step by step
sections.html:
Collect offers, choose one and sign a contract. The title company then runs a title search, finds any liens and proposes a closing date. You sign the deed at closing, and the title company pays off your mortgage and any tax balance from the sale money first, then hands you the rest.

With no buyer loan, nobody orders a lender appraisal, and nobody hands you an inspection repair list. Clear title still matters, so deal with liens early and disclose a tenant or an unpaid tax year upfront.

Before the closing date, ask the utility office to take a last reading and move the account out of your name. Keep a copy of every page you sign.

A tax debt will not stop a sale. The title company asks the county tax office for a payoff and deducts it from your check at closing. The lien attached January 1, so a bill that has not even been mailed yet is already tied to the house.

If you are behind, phone the Collin County tax office at 972-881-3014 before listing and request a written balance. Check with the appraisal district on which exemptions are filed for your account. A buyer moving in may claim a homestead for the rest of the year, and that can shrink the bill you two share.

Princeton's population jumped from 17,027 to an estimated 43,524 between the 2020 count and the 2025 estimate, and the new streets set the comparison for your house. A buyer touring a fresh subdivision will notice dated kitchens, worn flooring and deferred roof work in yours.

Decide early whether you will spend on repairs or sell as-is at a lower number. With a median household income of $105,200 and typical owned-home value of $331,000, many local buyers can afford newer construction, so an older house must justify its price. Sellers who skip repairs usually do better with an investor who prices the work in than with a retail buyer who demands it after inspection.

sections.h2: Papers to pull before you say yes
sections.html:
Three documents are worth having ready: the deed, the newest mortgage statement and a county tax balance.

Rank offers by the money you walk away with. A big retail price that comes with repair credits, concessions and months of waiting can leave you with less than a direct as-is sale closing on the day you pick. A cash buyer skips the lender appraisal and the repair haggling, though old taxes and liens still come out of your proceeds. Insist that each offer be written down with the price, who pays closing costs and the closing date.

faqs.a: Collin Central Appraisal District. Its site offers a property search, exemption forms and a taxing-entities page.

faqs.q: Where does a Princeton owner pay the county tax bill?
faqs.a: At the Collin County tax office in Plano, 900 E. Park Blvd, Ste 100. Call 972-881-3014 to confirm hours.

faqs.q: Is most Princeton housing owned or rented?
faqs.a: Owners hold most of it: 75.7% of homes are lived in by their owners, and rentals make up the rest.
Fast. The count was 6,807 in 2010, then 17,027 in 2020, with 43,524 estimated for 2025.

faqs.q: When do unpaid Texas property taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1 for most bills. From that date the unpaid amount grows with penalty and interest.
